description: Hand-labeled Rust verdict corpus: one-line edits in pinned real crates, each labeled with what the crate's own tests actually discriminate, so ripr's verdicts can be scored as false actionable, false exposed, false silent, abstained, or ideal.
label_method: For each case the edit was applied to the full pinned checkout, the crate's own test command was run to confirm the edit keeps tests green (behavior_preserving_rewrite) or breaks them (behavior_change), and each listed mutant of the edited expression was applied on top and the same test command run. A mutant counts as detected (`tests_failed`) when the test command fails after compiling. Each mutant was reviewed by hand for equivalence before its outcome counted. Truth is derived from the count of mutants with tests_failed: all is discriminated, none is not_discriminated, otherwise partially_discriminated.
verdict_projection: Only candidate_current findings on the anchor file and line count. exposed is credited; a named static_limit_kind or a no_static_path, infection_unknown, propagation_unknown or static_unknown class is limited; any other class (weakly_exposed, reachable_unrevealed) is a gap. A gap on the line outranks credit, and credit outranks a limit. No anchored finding is silent. The per-finding reading mirrors crates/ripr/src/output/human/triage.rs; the line-level precedence is this corpus's own policy.
non_claims: Rates describe this corpus only; they are not a population estimate for Rust code or for ripr in general.
Truth comes from the listed mutants, not from exhaustive mutation; a discriminated label means every listed mutant made the test command fail.
The harness runs ripr on retained upstream excerpts; excerpt findings matched the full pinned checkout at labeling time and must be re-checked when a verdict changes.
The harness does not run mutation testing, cargo test, or any network access.

cases.hard_case: serde's test_format_u8 checks all 256 u8 values with assert_eq! inside `loop`; the efficiency thread traced ripr's refusal to the loop and #[macro_use] mod rules, and the full repository also routes serde_core through a symlinked serde/src/core module.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 100 takes the two-digit branch and indexes the table past its end
not equivalent: 99 takes the three-digit branch and writes a leading zero

cases.reasoning: Every u8 value is formatted and compared with to_string(), so any boundary change at 100 fails test_format_u8. Withholding observation credit for an assertion inside a loop is a defensible static limit, but reporting reachable_unrevealed (a repairable gap with 'no assertion observes the changed behavior') is a false actionable verdict.

cases.hard_case: same exhaustive loop as the hundreds case, second boundary

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 10 takes the one-digit branch and writes ':'
not equivalent: 9 takes the two-digit branch and writes "09"

cases.reasoning: The exhaustive loop discriminates the tens boundary too. ripr reports propagation_unknown here, a limitation rather than a gap, which is an acceptable abstention.

cases.hard_case: tests live in tests/ and reach eval.rs only through the public VersionReq::matches API

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: ^1.2 stops matching 1.2.x
not equivalent: ^1.2 stops matching 1.3.0

cases.reasoning: test_caret asserts both matching and non-matching versions around ^1.2, so both mutants fail it. ripr names rust_integration_public_api_path_unresolved and stays limited, an acceptable abstention.

cases.hard_case: assertions go through tests/util assert_match_all/assert_match_none helpers

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: ~1.2.3-beta stops matching 1.2.3-beta
not equivalent: ~1.2.3-beta stops matching 1.2.4

cases.reasoning: test_tilde covers equal and later prereleases through helper assertions, so both mutants fail. ripr limits (infection_unknown and propagation_unknown), an acceptable abstention.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: <1.2.3-beta starts matching itself
not equivalent: later prereleases start matching

cases.reasoning: test_less_than checks prerelease ordering on both sides, so both mutants fail. ripr limits, an acceptable abstention.

cases.hard_case: the natural `<=` mutant is equivalent here because the branch only runs when the patches differ, so the corpus uses the negation

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: >1.2.3 starts matching 1.2.2 and stops matching 1.2.4

cases.reasoning: The negated comparison fails test_multiple. ripr limits on the unresolved public API path, an acceptable abstention.

cases.hard_case: same line as the first-run edit, scored here as a behavior-preserving rewrite with two mutants

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: '9' stops being a digit
not equivalent: ':' becomes a digit with value 10, but no test parses a ':' right after a number

cases.reasoning: Tests catch '9' being rejected but nothing exercises the byte just above '9', so the boundary is only partly discriminated. ripr's infection_unknown is an acceptable abstention; a gap naming the ':' input would be ideal.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a 31-comparator requirement is rejected
not equivalent: the limit check moves one comparator later

cases.reasoning: No test parses a requirement at the 31/32 comparator limit, so tightening the limit by one keeps the tests passing. ripr limits on the public API path, an acceptable abstention.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: ^0.1.x loses its minor-pinned branch
not equivalent: ^0.0.1 starts matching 0.0.2

cases.reasoning: Tests cover ^0.1.x but not that ^0.0.1 rejects a later patch, so the boundary is partly discriminated. ripr limits, an acceptable abstention.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: odd-length input reports the wrong error variant

cases.reasoning: test_invalid_length asserts Vec::from_hex("1") returns exactly OddLength, a straight-line assert_eq! on the error variant. ripr reports reachable_unrevealed and weakly_exposed on the line, a false actionable verdict.

cases.hard_case: straight-line assert_eq! in a #[cfg(test)] module; ripr still reports rust_assertion_context_unestablished

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: odd input is never rejected as OddLength

cases.reasoning: test_decode_to_slice asserts decode_to_slice(b"6", ..) is OddLength. ripr reports reachable_unrevealed with an unestablished assertion context, a false actionable verdict.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a longer output buffer is accepted
not equivalent: a shorter output buffer is accepted

cases.reasoning: Only the too-short buffer is tested, so accepting a too-long buffer keeps the tests passing. ripr's gap verdict is ideal, though its stated reason (unestablished assertion context) is not the real gap.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a too-long output buffer is accepted
not equivalent: a too-short output buffer is silently truncated

cases.reasoning: Only the too-long buffer is tested, so silent truncation into a short buffer keeps the tests passing. ripr's gap verdict is ideal.

cases.hard_case: tests are generated by a local test! macro_rules; ripr finds no related test

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a trailing 10 is written as ':'
not equivalent: a trailing 9 is written as "09"

cases.reasoning: The test! cases format 0, MIN and MAX values whose tail never lands on 9 or 10, so the tests still pass under both mutants. ripr's no_static_path is an acceptable abstention; a gap would be ideal.

cases.hard_case: one match arm carries four ranges; one test pins only 'a' and '-'

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: '_' stops being a word byte
not equivalent: 'a' stops being a word byte
not equivalent: 'Z' stops being a word byte

cases.reasoning: word_byte asserts only is_word_byte(b'a') and !is_word_byte(b'-'), so dropping '_' or 'Z' keeps the tests passing. ripr's weakly_exposed gap is ideal.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: U+07FF is no longer two-byte encodable
not equivalent: U+0800 becomes two-byte encodable

cases.reasoning: utf8::tests::bmp checks the encoded sequences across the BMP and fails on either side of 0x7FF. ripr's weakly_exposed gap is a false actionable verdict.

cases.hard_case: table-driven test: assert_eq! inside `for ... in &[...]` over a tuple table

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: lowercase renames produce uppercase
not equivalent: lowercase renames keep the original case

cases.reasoning: rename_variants compares every rule against an expected table, so both mutants fail. ripr's weakly_exposed gap is a false actionable verdict.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: UPPERCASE renames produce lowercase
not equivalent: UPPERCASE renames keep the original case

cases.reasoning: rename_fields compares every rule against an expected table, so both mutants fail. ripr's weakly_exposed gap is a false actionable verdict.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: "01" is accepted
not equivalent: "10" is rejected and "01" accepted

cases.reasoning: test_parse asserts the exact leading-zero error messages, so both mutants fail. ripr limits on the public API path, an acceptable abstention.

cases.hard_case: contradiction: reach says a related test reaches op() while related_tests_total is 0

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: ">=1.0" parses as Greater

cases.reasoning: Requirement parsing tests fail when '>=' parses as '>'. ripr reports reachable_unrevealed (a gap) with zero related tests, a false actionable verdict and an internal contradiction.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a remaining 1000 skips the four-digit loop
not equivalent: a remaining 999 is written with a leading zero

cases.reasoning: No test value leaves exactly 999 or 1000 for the loop, so the tests still pass under both mutants. ripr limits, an acceptable abstention.

cases.hard_case: first-run harness edit (PR #5286); 0.10.0 said reachable_unrevealed, 0.11 dev says infection_unknown

mutants.equivalence_review: the edit itself: '9' is no longer a digit

cases.reasoning: The edit breaks test_basic, test_caret, test_exact and test_multiple, so the existing tests discriminate it. 0.10's reachable_unrevealed was a false actionable verdict; 0.11 dev's infection_unknown is an acceptable abstention, and crediting the discriminator would be ideal.

cases.hard_case: first-run harness edit (PR #5286); 0.10.0 said weakly_exposed, 0.11 dev says infection_unknown

mutants.equivalence_review: the edit itself: exactly one unit formats as "1024 B" instead of "1.0 KiB"

cases.reasoning: The edit breaks tests::test_display and tests::test_to_string_as, which format exactly one unit. 0.10's weakly_exposed gap was a false actionable verdict; 0.11 dev's infection_unknown is an acceptable abstention.
